item.title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity
item.description:
ETAPS gradually prunes and adapts sparse models, keeping each step small so the model can recover quality without large optimizer states. It outperforms the previous state‑of‑the‑art at 50‑90% sparsity and reduces GPU‑time and memory by up to 49% and 5× respectively. This could help you run cheaper, high‑sparsity LLMs in production.

IT Breakdown: If you manage large language models, here is what to do: 1) Use ETAPS to prune in stages, 2) Keep the sparse delta small and train it continuously, 3) Monitor perplexity to ensure quality stays above baseline.

item.title: Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses
item.description:
This research shows how to pre‑process and organise knowledge into structured formats (like claim‑evidence trees, entity graphs, timelines) so that an AI agent’s search loop uses only the minimal necessary context, cutting query tokens by 91% and reducing latency from 140s to 30s. The authors built an open‑source pipeline called RAGFlow that turns a chaotic retrieval loop into five disciplined stations, giving the agent a curated, governed context instead of a raw ranked list of passages. For cloud infrastructure managers, this means a way to host and serve structured knowledge bases that improve agent efficiency and governance without adding new retrieval engines.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure, set up RAGFlow on your Kubernetes cluster: 1) ingest your documents into the compilation pipeline to generate claim‑evidence trees; 2) expose the compiled store via a REST API; 3) route your agents’ queries through the RAGFlow harness to cut token use and latency.

item.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
item.description:
SecPO introduces a new loss function and adversarial training pipeline that dramatically reduces prompt‑injection attack success rates on LLMs, while keeping normal performance intact. The researchers trained a Qwen‑3.6‑27B model with SecPO and strong synthetic attacks, cutting ASRs 1.5‑14.5× compared to previous methods and 2.4‑4.6× versus standard DPO loss. This shows a practical way to harden AI agents against injection attacks without hurting their usefulness.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud‑hosted AI services, run the SecPO training code on your models: 1) generate strong injected inputs with their AT pipeline, 2) fine‑tune your model using the SecPO loss, 3) test against known adaptive attacks. This will lower injection success rates and keep service quality high.

item.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
item.description:
ACCT lets you move the key‑value cache (the context) from a smaller LLM to a larger one without re‑running the original prompt, saving up to 20× faster inference and cutting memory use by 75%. They built three light components that pick useful tokens, decide how many to keep, and convert the cache into a format the target model can use. The result is that the larger model can infer faster and with fewer tokens, matching or beating its usual performance.

IT Breakdown: If you manage multi‑model LLM deployments, step 1: identify which models in your stack can be paired for cross‑cache transfer; step 2: apply a KV selector to keep only the most relevant context tokens within your budget; step 3: convert and load the sparse KV into the target model before inference. This can cut inference time and memory in your cloud infra.

item.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
item.description:
Flide is an inference engine that speeds up decision‑making models by avoiding redundant calculation and keeping results mathematically exact. It does this by flattening token streams and using GPU‑based indices to fork attention across different decision branches, allowing up to 9.5× faster queries than existing engines while maintaining precision. This means faster, more accurate LLM‑driven decision systems for applications that need low latency and high reliability.

IT Breakdown: If you manage LLM‑based decision systems, step 1: replace your current inference engine with Flide; step 2: update your deployment to use the flattened token stream format; step 3: test performance and precision against your baseline, aiming for up to 9.5× speed improvement without sacrificing accuracy.

item.title: [News] Supermarket freezers across Europe hit by second suspected cyber-attack
item.description: Supermarket chains across Europe have experienced a second suspected cyber‑attack that remotely hijacked refrigeration and freezer systems, raising temperatures and causing significant food losses. The incidents mirror a larger French attack that exploited vulnerabilities in Danfoss controllers, highlighting the risks of connected IoT devices in retail environments.

item.title: [News] Omen AI adds liquid know-how in $16 million Aquatic Labs acquisition
item.description: Omen AI has acquired Aquatic Labs for $16 million, combining real‑time water‑sensor technologies to monitor cooling fluids in data centers. The merged solution promises instant detection of valve failure and bacterial contamination, aiming to reduce costly downtime and water waste.

item.title: [News] Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
item.description: A network of over 400 AI-powered apps, including Viefur, covertly generate sexually abusive deepfake content when accessed under certain conditions. The apps, linked to Chinese developers, bypass platform policies and are promoted via Meta ads, raising serious regulatory and security concerns.

item.title: [News] Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
item.description: The article explains how AI coding agents consume significantly more tokens per task than simple chat prompts, as they plan, generate code, run tests, and iterate to fix errors. It highlights that as agents become more capable, their token usage—and potentially cost—will increase dramatically.

item.title: [News] The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
item.description: MIT Tech Review discusses the emergence of the agentic web—a future where autonomous software agents navigate the internet—highlighting its potential to transform online interactions.
